model_fitness.best_available_model: Patient-derived cells carrying the actual exon 55 nonsense allele: urine-derived renal epithelial cells or MYOD1-transdifferentiated/immortalized patient myoblasts differentiated to myotubes, paired with a dual-luciferase PTC reporter carrying the patient's exon 55 stop codon plus ~12 nt of native flanking context.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the two gating steps. The patient myotube captures NMD of the mutant transcript and endogenous readthrough-to-protein in a cell that transcribes full-length DMD (EVIDENCE that readthrough can yield dystrophin protein in human nonsense DMD: PMID 24349052). The reporter isolates codon-context permissiveness, which is the dominant determinant of readthrough efficiency (EVIDENCE: PMID 40156864).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partial. Myotubes are the correct Dp427m-expressing lineage; urine-derived cells are not muscle but are adequate for allele-specific transcript/NMD measurement. Cardiomyocytes and CNS neurons (Dp140) are not represented.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: (1) Absolute and allele-specific DMD transcript abundance by ddPCR/RT-qPCR +/- NMD inhibition (cycloheximide or SMG1 inhibitor) as the NMD-efficiency readout; (2) readthrough ratio in the dual-luciferase reporter with ataluren dose-response, G418 as positive control, and ataluren+G418 combination; (3) full-length dystrophin protein by capillary/Western and sarcolemmal immunostaining in treated myotubes.
model_fitness.important_limitations: Myotube cultures lack contraction-induced sarcolemmal stress, so they cannot report functional benefit; dystrophin levels in vitro do not predict the clinical dystrophin-quantity threshold; no exon-55-specific NMD or readthrough data exist in retrieved literature (EVIDENCE, inconclusive: PubMed search, this session), so this is a first-in-allele measurement; reporter context is a surrogate for the native 11.5 kb transcript.

plan.critical_question: Does enough exon 55 mutant DMD mRNA escape nonsense-mediated decay to serve as template, and is this exact stop codon plus flanking context readthrough-permissive enough for ataluren (alone or combined) to produce detectable full-length dystrophin?
plan.proposed_experiment: Two-arm bench package, 6-10 weeks. Arm A (template): derive urine epithelial cells and/or patient myoblasts, differentiate to myotubes, measure DMD transcript abundance by ddPCR against 2-3 control lines, and repeat under NMD blockade (cycloheximide, SMG1 inhibitor) to quantify the NMD-sensitive fraction. Arm B (permissiveness): build a dual-luciferase reporter containing the patient's exon 55 PTC with native flanking nucleotides; run ataluren dose-response, G418 positive control, and ataluren+G418 combination (design per PMID 40156864). Confirmatory step: treat patient myotubes with the best-performing condition and quantify full-length dystrophin protein and sarcolemmal localisation.
plan.model: Patient-derived myotubes (and urine-derived cells) plus patient-sequence dual-luciferase PTC reporter; control lines from unaffected donors and from a known ataluren-responsive nonsense DMD allele as a benchmark.
plan.primary_readout: Primary: readthrough ratio (reporter) and full-length dystrophin protein in treated patient myotubes, expressed as % of normal control. Co-primary gate: mutant DMD transcript abundance as % of control and the magnitude of its increase under NMD blockade.
plan.supportive_result: Mutant transcript is >=25-30% of control (modest NMD) AND ataluren produces a dose-dependent reporter readthrough comparable to a known responsive allele AND detectable full-length dystrophin appears at the myotube membrane. This supports proceeding to ataluren treatment under existing access pathways with dystrophin/biopsy or MRI-based monitoring, and makes the combination fallback unnecessary.
plan.negative_result: Mutant transcript is severely depleted (<10% of control) and/or reporter readthrough with ataluren is at assay baseline while G418 shows signal only at toxic concentrations, and no dystrophin protein is detectable. That means the codon context or the missing template is the binding constraint: deprioritise ataluren monotherapy and redirect to agents that address template (NMD attenuation as a tool) or to a higher-efficiency readthrough mechanism such as an engineered suppressor tRNA.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to commit this patient/stratum to small-molecule readthrough at all, versus declaring the allele readthrough-refractory. This single experiment, not more literature, decides the arm; it also produces the template measurement that gates both other modalities, so run it first regardless of which arm is favoured.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Same patient-derived myotube system as the small-molecule arm, used as a tool-compound testbed: steric-block 2'-MOE/PMO ASOs tiled across the exon 55 PTC region and the downstream exon-junction-complex deposition site, with siRNA/ASO knockdown of UPF1 or SMG1 as the mechanistic positive control.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Partial only, and the mismatch is conceptual rather than technical. The model can measure whether raising mutant transcript abundance increases dystrophin output when combined with a readthrough agent. It cannot test a standalone oligonucleotide therapy because no oligonucleotide chemistry can force ribosomal readthrough; readthrough is a release-factor event (INFERENCE, contradictory, from mechanism described in PMID 40156864).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partial. Correct lineage for Dp427m; cardiomyocytes, where the approved DMD oligonucleotides essentially fail to distribute, are not represented, and that is precisely the tissue where this modality's ceiling is lowest (EVIDENCE, contradictory: NCT03907072 suvodirsen Phase 2/3 failure for lack of efficacy).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Mutant DMD transcript abundance (fold-increase over untreated), and dystrophin protein in the ASO+readthrough-agent combination versus readthrough agent alone. Secondary: genome-wide stabilisation of physiological NMD substrates by RNA-seq as an on-target liability readout.
model_fitness.important_limitations: In vitro free uptake (gymnosis/transfection) massively overstates in vivo myofiber nuclear delivery; the model cannot address the actual gating problem, which is that a template-raising agent has no standalone benefit and would carry full systemic oligonucleotide toxicity. Nonspecific NMD suppression liability is only crudely captured in a dish.

plan.critical_question: Is template abundance, rather than readthrough efficiency, the rate-limiting variable for dystrophin restoration at this allele? Only if the answer is yes does any oligonucleotide have a job here, and even then only as an adjuvant.
plan.proposed_experiment: Run this strictly as a conditional, cheap add-on to the small-molecule gating experiment and only if Arm A shows the exon 55 transcript is substantially NMD-depleted. In patient myotubes, use UPF1/SMG1 knockdown (siRNA or gapmer) as a mechanistic ceiling test: if restoring transcript abundance to near-control levels, in combination with ataluren or G418, does not increase full-length dystrophin protein, stop. If it does, then and only then synthesise a small tiled set of steric-block ASOs across the PTC/downstream EJC region to ask whether sequence-specific NMD evasion can reproduce the knockdown effect without global NMD suppression, with RNA-seq of canonical NMD substrates as the specificity readout.
plan.model: Patient-derived myotubes carrying the exon 55 PTC; UPF1/SMG1 knockdown as positive control for template elevation; isotype/scrambled ASO and untreated controls.
plan.primary_readout: Fold-increase in full-length dystrophin protein for (template-raising agent + readthrough agent) versus readthrough agent alone, in the same cells on the same blot.
plan.supportive_result: Template elevation produces a clear supra-additive increase in dystrophin protein, and a steric-block ASO reproduces most of that gain with minimal stabilisation of unrelated NMD substrates. Decision: keep the ASO as a research tool compound to define the template ceiling and to size the combination effect; do not advance it as a therapeutic on its own.
plan.negative_result: Transcript abundance rises severalfold with no corresponding increase in dystrophin protein, or the exon 55 transcript was never NMD-limited in Arm A. Decision: close the oligonucleotide arm for this hypothesis. Readthrough efficiency, not template, is limiting, and the modality is mechanistically incapable of addressing it.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to spend anything at all on oligonucleotide chemistry for this hypothesis. The honest default is no: no agent of any maturity targets translation termination, no NMD-inhibitor oligonucleotide has entered clinical development for any indication, and the realistic best case is a tool compound, not a drug. The experiment exists to kill the arm quickly and cheaply, or to justify it narrowly as an adjuvant.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Two-stage model. Stage 1 (mechanism, adequate): anticodon-engineered, site-specifically modified suppressor tRNA matched to the exon 55 stop codon, transfected into patient-derived myotubes, mirroring the design validated for CFTR nonsense mutations where m1A-modified sup-tRNA improved readthrough, aminoacylation and persistence and restored function in organoids and mouse lung (EVIDENCE: PMID 42658930). Stage 2 (delivery, inadequate): no validated muscle- or cardiomyocyte-tropic LNP for tRNA cargo was retrieved; the CF proof-of-concept required bespoke pulmonary LNP engineering and local airway access, and lung tropism does not transfer to myofibers (EVIDENCE, contradictory: PMID 42658930).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for mechanism in Stage 1: the sup-tRNA acts at the ribosome and restores authentic full-length Dp427m, avoiding the unresolved multi-exon-skip question entirely (INFERENCE, supportive). No for the actual gating question, which is systemic biodistribution to ~30-40% of body mass plus myocardium.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partial. Patient myotubes are the right lineage for mechanism; cardiomyocytes, diaphragm and satellite cells are the cells that decide translational viability and are not captured in vitro. An mdx-background mouse carrying a nonsense allele plus a dystrophin-independent reporter PTC would be needed for the delivery question.
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Stage 1: full-length dystrophin protein and sarcolemmal DGC reassembly (beta-dystroglycan, nNOS relocalisation) in treated patient myotubes, plus readthrough selectivity at normal stop codons by ribosome profiling or proteomics. Stage 2: fraction of dystrophin-positive fibers across quadriceps, diaphragm and heart after systemic LNP dosing, and dystrophin as % of wild-type by Western.
model_fitness.important_limitations: tRNA is a short-lived, non-replicating cargo, implying chronic high-frequency LNP redosing in a lifelong whole-body myopathy, with innate-immune and tolerability ceilings (INFERENCE, contradictory). Intramuscular dosing can demonstrate proof-of-mechanism in one muscle but cannot model a systemic myopathy. No DMD sup-tRNA clinical program exists (EVIDENCE, contradictory: ClinicalTrials.gov search, DMD + tRNA, this session), so there is no human safety precedent.

plan.critical_question: Can any systemically administered RNA formulation deliver a suppressor tRNA to a therapeutically meaningful fraction of skeletal myofibers AND cardiomyocytes? Mechanism is not the open question here; biodistribution is.
plan.proposed_experiment: Invert the usual order and test delivery before investing in cargo optimisation. Formulate a readily available reporter RNA cargo of comparable size and chemistry to a modified sup-tRNA in a panel of candidate LNPs (hepatotropic benchmark plus muscle-biased lipid compositions) and dose dystrophic mice intravenously. Quantify cargo delivery and functional readthrough per tissue using a PTC reporter readout in quadriceps, diaphragm and heart versus liver. In parallel, run the cheap Stage 1 mechanism test: transfect a modified sup-tRNA designed against the patient's exon 55 codon into patient myotubes and ask whether full-length dystrophin and sarcolemmal DGC reassembly appear.
plan.model: Dystrophic mouse (mdx background) for systemic biodistribution/functional readthrough per tissue; patient-derived exon 55 myotubes for the mechanism arm. Liver serves as the internal positive control for LNP function.
plan.primary_readout: Primary: functional readthrough per gram of tissue in heart and diaphragm, expressed as a fraction of the liver signal from the same animal. Secondary: % dystrophin-positive fibers and dystrophin as % of wild-type. Mechanism arm: full-length dystrophin in patient myotubes.
plan.supportive_result: At least one formulation achieves a readthrough signal in heart and diaphragm within roughly one order of magnitude of liver at tolerated doses, while the myotube arm shows sup-tRNA-dependent full-length dystrophin with DGC reassembly. Decision: invest in cargo chemistry and durability, and begin defining a redosing interval.
plan.negative_result: All formulations remain overwhelmingly hepatotropic with heart and diaphragm signal at or near background, even though the mechanism arm succeeds in the dish. Decision: do not pursue sup-tRNA as a therapeutic for this patient; the agent would work in vitro, reach liver in vivo, and never achieve myofiber or cardiomyocyte exposure. Keep the mechanism result as a reusable asset and re-evaluate only when a muscle-tropic delivery platform is independently validated.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to fund an RNA program now or shelve it pending delivery. Running the delivery test first prevents the predictable failure mode of a correct mechanism with no route to the tissue, and the myotube mechanism arm is cheap enough to run alongside so that a shelved program is shelved with a known-good cargo design rather than an untested one.
